channel.title: The Catholic Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Catholic Review (catholicreview.org)

item.title: Judge cites Gospel verses in releasing 5-year-old and father from immigrant detention
item.description: A federal judge cited two Gospel verses in his order releasing 5-year-old Liam Conejo Ramos and his father, who had been detained by immigration agents in a Minneapolis suburb and sent to a Texas family detention center.

item.title: Pope Leo laments rising U.S.-Cuba tensions, calls for ‘sincere’ dialogue
item.description: Pope Leo XIV has called for "a sincere and effective dialogue" as tensions between the U.S. and Cuba mount.

item.title: Archbishop Lori joins local clergy decrying violence connected to immigration enforcement
item.description: Archbishop William E. Lori joined the growing chorus of prelates denouncing violence in the United States connected to immigration enforcement.

item.title: Radio Interview: Notre Dame of Maryland partners with senior living community
item.description: Catholic Review Managing Editor George Matysek speaks with Dr. Mary Lou Yam, president of Notre Dame of Maryland University, and Austin Koo, development director at Brightview Senior Living, about a long-planned partnership that will bring a senior living community to the university’s campus. The project will create housing for independent living, assisted living and memory care while opening the door to intergenerational learning.

item.title: Pope welcomes new Marian mosaic, St. Rose of Lima statue in Vatican Gardens
item.description: The Vatican Gardens welcomed a new Marian mosaic and a statue of St. Rose of Lima, both created by young artists from Peru -- in a ceremony that clearly delighted Pope Leo XIV -- an American-born pope that holds Peru in "a special place" in his heart.

item.title: Movie Review: ‘Mercy’
item.description: With apologies to pulp fiction crime writer Mickey Spillane, the dystopian thriller "Mercy" (Amazon MGM) might more aptly be called AI the Jury. That's because, in the film's near-future setting, artificial intelligence is empowered to fight crime by generating a rough sort of justice.

item.title: Minneapolis priest ‘not hopeful’ tensions will ease under border czar
item.description: A Minneapolis priest told OSV News that despite signals of deescalation, tensions over immigration enforcement actions in that city will not see the situation get "better in a few days."

item.title: Pope Leo prays for thousands affected by disastrous floods in southern Africa
item.description: As deadly floods hit southern Africa, Pope Leo XIV prayed for the affected, with Catholic bishops in the region urging support for thousands struck by the climate change-related disaster.

item.title: Guatemala’s ‘Fray Augusto’ is a martyr of the confessional, vice postulator says
item.description: At first glance, the official photo of Venerable Augusto Ramírez Monasterio -- known simply as "Fray Augusto" -- shows a smiling Franciscan friar standing in a small garden, hands clasped and slightly hidden within the sleeves of his brown habit.

item.title: Happiness cannot be bought, hoarded, only shared with others, pope says
item.description: A lack of faith in Christ leads to many delusions, such as believing the arrogant will always rule and only money can buy happiness, Pope Leo XIV said.
